title: Eleven Words and One Envelope
subtitle: 祝贺与礼仪 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 祝贺与礼仪（社会服务与人际沟通·祝贺与礼仪）
meta: 主题语境：祝贺与礼仪（社会服务与人际沟通·祝贺与礼仪）　|　核心词汇：congratulation　|　正文 330 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 congratulation 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 my aunt ① sent a congratulation to a girl she had never met, and she said the sending was the whole of the news. The ② congratulation, meaning the words and not the envelope, ran to eleven words and stayed that length; congratulation, she said, is the only thing in a post that is judged by how soon it is sent.

Every ③ congratulation in that house had the same handwriting, and the ④ congratulation at the end, meaning the one she kept for the wedding and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever kept twice. Congratulation, my mother said, is nine parts handwriting and one part somebody willing to send it; my aunt said the sending is the part that fills the envelope.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ congratulation was the whole of the evening, meaning the praise and not the note. The ⑥ congratulation, meaning the praise and not any of that, is the only thing in an evening that everybody wants and nobody writes down; congratulation, he said, is either something you send or the only word that means both a note and a praise. She said the praise is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ congratulation had become a line in a card, and the card had become an argument about the handwriting. The ⑧ congratulation of the whole thing, my aunt wrote in July, was one envelope and thirty years of sending; congratulation, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to send it. He said the sending was never mentioned.

The ⑨ congratulation I remember is the one at the end, which she sent in 1978 and is still described as the shortest in the county. A ⑩ congratulation, my mother said in 1980, is the only thing that improves by being sent; every congratulation, she said, is a praise that has agreed to look like a note. She said the praise was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 祝贺（指那些贺词本身，与那个信封相对）
C. 固定搭配：send a congratulation 发出祝贺
D. n. 祝贺（指那栋房子里每一封贺词）
E. n. 祝贺（指末尾那一封）
F. n. 称赞；赞许（抽象：口头的称许）
G. n. 祝贺（指贺卡里提到的那一句）
H. n. 祝贺（抽象总称，congratulations 常用复数）

items.q: sent a congratulation to a girl she had never met
The congratulation, meaning the words and not the envelope
congratulation was the whole of the evening
the congratulation had become a line in a card
The congratulation of the whole thing
A congratulation, my mother said in 1980

answers.why: send a congratulation 意为“发出祝贺”，1964 年姑姑给一个她从未见过的姑娘发出了祝贺。
congratulation 意为“祝贺”，指那些贺词本身而不是那个信封，只有十一个词。
congratulation 指那栋房子里每一封贺词，每一封都是同样的笔迹。
congratulation 指末尾那一封（她留给婚礼的那一封），是唯一有人留过两次的。
congratulation 意为“称赞、赞许”，父亲说称赞就是那个傍晚的全部，指的是口头的称许而不是那张便条。
congratulation 为抽象用法，指那份称赞而不是那张便条，是傍晚里人人都想要、却无人写下来的东西。
congratulation 意为“祝贺”，指贺卡里提到的那一句，到 1972 年这句祝贺成了贺卡里的一行。
congratulation 意为“祝贺”，姑姑七月写道，整件事的祝贺是一个信封三十年的寄送。
congratulation 意为“祝贺、恭喜”，我记得的是末尾那一封，她 1978 年寄出，至今仍被说成全县最短的。
congratulation 为抽象总称，母亲说一句祝贺是唯一会因为被寄出而变好的东西。
